findings.title: Theorem2.1 termination tuple omits the identity-height coordinate n0
findings.claim_checked: Every prescribed rank-two valley replacement strictly decreases the printed tuple (n1,...,n_ell(g)).
assumptions_checked: W=(C2 x C2)*C2, gens s,t,u and st=ts only cross-generator relation
(s,id,t) embedded geodesic in P(g); (s,st,t) is precisely the permitted alternate square path
findings.counterexample: Printed (2,0,0) changes to (2,1,0), hence increases lexicographically.
findings.verified_repair: Use (n0,n1,...,n_ell(g)); valley removal lowers its first changed coordinate; new interiors have greater height; loop-erasure cannot increase coordinates. Finite P(g) and embedded paths give finitely many tuples. Termination leads to a common weak-order upper bound for every pair, hence a largest point.
findings.counterevidence: In the actual example p(g)=st exists. Rank-three lemma and residue-invariance checks retain all geometric steps. No theorem counterexample was found.
findings.severity_reason: The demonstrated invalid termination step occurs in Theorem 2.1, which supplies the projection used by the core normal-form construction. The complete verified repair does not erase the original proof defect; no theorem counterexample is asserted.
findings.core_dependency: Local termination justification within the proof of the largest-element projection theorem, feeding the normal-form construction.

problems.independent_check: For W=(C2 x C2)*C2 with st=ts and g=stu, exact reduced words stu,tsu give [id,g]={id,s,t,st,stu}; the final u bridge is the unique closest wall, so P(g)={id,s,t,st}. The permitted square replacement (s,id,t)->(s,st,t) changes the printed tuple (2,0,0)->(2,1,0), increasing it. Adding n0 changes (1,2,0,0)->(0,2,1,0). In general the first altered coordinate is the valley height; opposite-path interiors have greater height, loop erasure cannot increase counts, and finite embedded paths give termination.
problems.assumptions: Finite generating set, genuine weak-order interval, correct nearest-wall set, entire embedded path and prescribed rank-two replacement checked; not an arbitrary height sequence.
problems.core_dependency: Theorem2.1 projection existence supplies the recursive normal form in the main biautomaticity proof. Its invalid original termination argument is Major under 0.7.1 even though the complete n0 repair is verified.
problems.counterevidence: The example has p(g)=st; no counterexample to projection existence or biautomaticity. Corrected proof preserves the geometric invariant.
